title: rotation-handbook-dashboard-personas-and-trace-notes
content:
Purpose
This is a working handbook for rotation owners to quickly pick the right dashboard, apply a lightweight metric annotator, and use trace-sampling heuristics suited to the incident severity and investigation scope. Focus is on pragmatic, compact workflows rather than exhaustive signal lists.

High-level goals
- Make oncall handoffs low-friction via persona-specific dashboard entry points.
- Standardize a short investigation checklist (first 6 actions) so non-experts can triage and escalate faster.
- Provide trace sampling and short-term query-budget guidance to keep incident analysis cost-effective.
- Capture a minimal annotator convention for panels and traces so investigations are communicable.

Intended audience
- Tier 1 oncall (frontend operators, basic troubleshooting)
- Tier 2 SRE (deep trace + access to KV cache views)
- Product engineer/owner (impact and rollback decisions)
- Rotation lead (post-incident coordination, follow-ups)

Persona entry points (wireframes, quick descriptions)
1) Pager-first (Tier 1)
  - One-line symptom summary on top.
  - Key SLO panel (error rate, p99 latency) with red/yellow banding.
  - Recent deploys and canary flags (last 30 minutes).
  - Quick filters: tenant id, route, model family.
  - Action buttons: warm-restart stream, toggle lightweight fallback route (if bound to user).

2) Session-rebuild (Tier 2)
  - Session reconstruction widget (request timeline, leading prompts, cache hits).
  - KV cache warmth heatmap by model and tenant.
  - Span density histogram (microcalls per request).
  - Trace sample livestream (severity-weighted sampling, see tracing heuristics).

3) Cost-focus (Rotation lead / Product)
  - Token spend delta by route and model.
  - Query cost per 5m bucket + anomaly detector.
  - Top 10 costly tenants + sample request IDs.

Metric annotator conventions (compact)
- Prefixes: op_ for operational counters, lat_ for latency quantiles, cost_ for billing-related metrics.
- Units: explicit suffixes where ambiguous (e.g., lat_p95_ms, cost_per_1000_tokens_usd).
- Panel titles: <persona> - <topline metric> - <scope> (example: pager - error-rate - global 5m).
- Annotation layer: deploy id and rollout percentage are shown above timeseries. If absent, assume not-deployed in window.
- Tag canonicalization: tenant_id, route, model_id, cache_state (hit|miss|warm|cold).

First-6 investigation steps (fast path)
1) Check SLOs and topline error-rate panel; confirm scope (global vs single tenant).
2) Look at recent deploys / rollouts; if deploy overlap with onset, file as deploy-correlated.
3) Compare cache warmth and cold-start rate in same window.
4) Pull 2-3 representative traces using severity-weighted selector (see below).
5) If traces show repeated microcall failures, escalate to model-onboarding team and flag as potential model regression.
6) If no traces or inconclusive, widen sampling window and run synthetic probe to reproduce.

Trace sampling heuristics (practical rules)
- Severity-weighted sampling: sample ratio proportional to error score (0.5% normal, 5% on high error bursts). Increase only for 30m windows and then revert.
- Session anchors: for multi-turn chats, always capture initial prompt + last two turns. Avoid entire session unless debugging context propagation.
- KV cache focused traces: when investigating cold starts, prioritize traces where cache_state=miss and model_id is heavy (gptx/xxl).
- Budgeting: keep ad-hoc trace capture under 10k spans/day per rotation. For deep hunts, request temporary budget via JIRA and document scope.

Dashboard widgets to build (implementation notes)
- Compact SLO bar: single row showing current burn rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, and token spend with hover drilldowns.
- Tenant focus card: quick switcher with last 20 requests and a link to request replay console.
- Timeline correlator: stacked lanes for deploys, infra scaling events, and KV eviction spikes.
- Trace-sampler status: small widget showing current sample rate and reason tag (manual|auto|severity).

Query budgeting and cost guardrails
- Default dashboard queries must timeout at 30s and limit results to 500 rows.
- Long-running forensic queries should be run in the telemetry sandbox or requested via ticket.
- For rotation-driven deep dives, use the cost-focus dashboard which shows projected token spend if current rate persists for 24h.

Example scenarios (short)
A) Sudden spike in p99 latency (global)
  - Pager opens latency panel -> see spike coincident with autoscaler activity.
  - Check session-rebuild; find increase in microcall retries -> escalate to runtime team.
B) Error-rate up for one tenant
  - Use tenant focus card -> sample 5 traces with severity-weighting -> identify malformed prompt causing parser layer to throw 400 -> patch in product lib, roll forward canary.

Annotations and post-incident notes protocol
- Rotation lead adds a 1-paragraph incident summary into the dashboard annotation with JIRA id and initial hypothesis.
- All traces used for the write-up should be linked in the investigation ticket; sensitive data redaction note must be included.

Open questions / TODOs
- Can we add an inline quick playback for sampled traces (mocked UI exists but not wired). (Owner: Miguel)
- Define automatic revert policy for sample rate increases older than 30 minutes. (Owner: Priya)
- Build a minimal training slide for Tier 1 rotations on using the persona entry points. (Owner: Evan)

References and quick links
- CON-OBS-1423 (dashboard permission changes)
- JIRA-OPS-578 (temporary trace budget request)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/234 (tenant focus card prototype)

Notes to self (working fragments)
- keep the persona panels to 4 or fewer for a quick glance.
- prefer visual banding over numeric thresholds for oncall readability.
- need to review retention impact of session-replay snapshots.

If you're on rotation and not sure where to start: open the pager-first view, run the first-6 checklist, grab 3 traces, and post links into the incident ticket. Escalate after step 4 if root cause unclear or if cost impact exceeds 1% of daily token spend.
